segments.text: Hi, I'm Adam Rosie. How are you getting on at UWE?
Thank you for coming to this tutorial.
This is an opportunity for you to discuss any problems you might be having with your studies.
Well, I've been very busy with settling in and doing assignments.
It's also different here in the UK to living and working in my country.
How do you find working with British and other international students?
Well, it's been a new kind of experience for me, living and studying with students from different cultures.
think it teaches us how to be tolerant of them. You know how to give and take so
that we can all work and live together. Sometimes there are disagreements but
then we have to try to solve the problems. But in general I'm finding it a
great experience. Yes me too. It's really fun. However I am having problems
understanding some of the lectures. Oh do you think that's because the
tutors speak too fast, or there is background noise from outside, or perhaps noises inside
the room like students talking or coughing?
Well, all those things could happen, but often it's because the lecturers use a lot of technical
vocabulary, or use familiar vocabulary in a way that I don't understand. However, individual
lecturers have different ways of making the lecture clearer. For example, some of my
engineering lecturers use diagrams and graphics to show how different sections
of the topic are connected which makes it much easier for us to follow the
lecture. We also sometimes get pre-lecture notes before the lecture and
these are really helpful. So is there any advice that you wish you'd had at the
beginning of your course? Rosie what about you? Well I find it very strange
lectures where the lecturer expects the audience to contribute to the
lecture and ask questions. This would never happen at my home university. The
lecturer would not expect to be interrupted by the students. Also in my
country no one is allowed into the lecture theatre late or to fall asleep
during the lecture. I think international students should be more prepared for the
lecture conventions before they arrive in the UK or in the induction week maybe.
There's so much for them to take in during the first week of the course they
can't take it all in at once. Okay that's interesting. Now what about study groups?
Students are sometimes advised to form study groups with others on the course.
Have you ever done that? Was it helpful? Yes I have worked as part of a study
group, but I think it's best to work with people who have similar study habits as my
own, and if possible with people who live quite near. I find it difficult to form groups
with the English students, though, and I only seem to study with other international students.
Some interesting points there, Ahmad.
